methodologyNotes: Covers standalone audio mixing consoles and desks sold at a published US price, spanning analog and digital models for live sound, studio recording, streaming, and podcast production. Excludes DJ performance mixers, computer software mixers, and rack/plug-in signal processors. Price is typical US MSRP in USD. type is analog or digital. totalInputChannels is the manufacturer's stated total number of input channels on the console. micPreamps is the count of dedicated XLR microphone preamp inputs. phantomPower is global (a single 48V switch feeding all mic inputs), per-channel, or none. eqBandsPerChannel is the number of EQ bands on a mono input channel (e.g. 3 for a 3-band EQ); 0 if input channels have no EQ. auxSends is the number of independent aux send buses. usbRecordChannels is the number of discrete audio channels the mixer streams to a computer over USB (2 for a stereo interface, higher for multitrack); 0 if there is no built-in USB audio interface. builtInEffects is the count of onboard DSP effect programs/presets; 0 if none. onboardRecording is true if the unit records audio to internal or SD-card storage without a computer. faderLengthMm is channel fader travel in millimeters; 0 if the mixer uses rotary level knobs only. weightKg is unit weight in kilograms.

products.name: Yamaha MG10XU
products.priceNote: Broadcasters General Store (bgs.cc) product page lists "MSRP: $383.00" for the Yamaha MG10XU (its own selling price shown as "Now: $294.99"). Reported priceUsd = 383 as the stated US MSRP.
products.provenance: Yamaha's official MG Series (XU/X) specifications page contains a per-model comparison table; the MG10XU column was identified unambiguously as the USB-equipped 10-input model (its "Digital I/O" cell reads "USB Audio Class 2.0 compliant" while the adjacent non-USB MG10X reads "-", and its output/noise rows reference a "STEREO LEVEL knob" rather than a fader), confirming +48V phantom power, SPX algorithm 24 programs, 4 mono MIC/LINE preamps, AUX SEND 1, rotary level knobs (no faders), and 2.1 kg net weight. Broadcasters General Store (bgs.cc) corroborates the exact product "Yamaha MG10XU 10 Channel Analog Mixer," listing MSRP $383.00 and a matching MG10XU spec block (10 channels = 4 mono + 3 stereo, "USB Audio (MG10XU) 2 IN / 2 OUT," SPX 24 programs, +48V phantom). Front End Audio (fetched separately) further states the MG10XU "featuring 3-band equalizers on all mono channels," supporting eqBandsPerChannel = 3.

products.name: Mackie ProFX10v3
products.priceNote: No US MSRP in USD could be sourced from a fetched page. Mackie's official product page listed no price ("On Backorder" / "Find a dealer"). Every US retailer attempted (Sweetwater, B&H, Amazon, Guitar Center, Walmart, Reverb, zZounds) returned HTTP 403 / bot-wall. The Thomann UK retailer page listed the ProFX10v3 at £193 incl. VAT, which is a UK price (not a US MSRP in USD), so priceUsd is left null rather than performing a currency-conversion guess.
products.provenance: The official Mackie product page (source) confirms the exact model "ProFX10v3 — 10-Channel Professional Analog Mixer with USB", stating a 10-channel analog USB mixer with four Onyx mic preamps, 3-band EQ on all channels, 48V phantom power on all channels, and a GigFX engine with 24 effects; it displayed no price ("On Backorder" / "Find a dealer"). The Thomann UK retailer page (corroboration) independently confirms the same ProFX10v3 and adds weight 2.2 kg, a single aux send ("Aux Ways 1"), a 2-in/4-out USB interface with 2-channel recording and "Multitrack Recording: No" / "USB/SD Direct Record: No", plus "Available since December 2019". No US-dollar price was obtainable because all fetched US retailers returned 403/bot-walls, so priceUsd and faderLengthMm (not stated on either page) are left null.

products.name: Behringer Xenyx X1204USB
products.priceNote: Thomann US storefront (thomannmusic.com, page served for United States in USD) lists the Behringer Xenyx X1204 USB at "$152" verbatim; used as typical US street price. Behringer's official product page shows no price/MSRP.
products.provenance: Behringer's official product page (source) confirms the exact model "XENYX X1204USB" as a "Premium 12-Input 2/2-Bus Mixer" with 4 onboard XENYX mic preamps, "British" channel EQ, a 24-bit Multi-FX processor with 16 editable presets, and a bi-directional stereo USB/audio interface; it lists no price. The Thomann retailer page (corroboration) is for the same exact "Behringer Xenyx X1204 USB" and states, verbatim, 12 channels, 4 mic inputs with 3-band EQ and switchable 48 V phantom power, 60 mm faders, 2 AUX sends, a USB audio interface with 2 inputs / 2 outputs and "USB/SD Direct Record: No", 16 FX presets, and a price of "$152" (available since February 2010). weightKg was left null because Thomann self-conflicts (bullet "2.8 kg" vs spec-table "3,8 kg") and no clean period-formatted kg value could be sourced.

products.name: Allen & Heath ZED-24
products.priceNote: proacousticsusa.com lists "MSRP: $1,499.99" (with a discounted street price of "$1,199.99"); frontendaudio.com sells the same unit at "$1,199.99". Used the stated MSRP of $1,499.99 per the "typical US MSRP" methodology.
products.provenance: The official Allen & Heath page (allen-heath.com) returned HTTP 403 and its user-guide PDF was non-extractable, so I sourced from two independent authorized US dealers reproducing the manufacturer's data. proacousticsusa.com confirms the exact model (Model #: ZED-24, Part #: ZED24, SKU AH-ZED24) and gives the full spec sheet used here: "16 mic/line inputs", "Responsive 3-band, swept mid EQ with MusiQ", "4 aux sends", "USB 1.1 compliant 16bit" stereo audio, "100mm professional quality faders", "Weight (Unpacked) 10.5kg", and a listed "MSRP: $1,499.99" (street $1,199.99). frontendaudio.com corroborates the identical ZED-24 spec set (16 mono channels, 3-band EQ, 4 auxes, ALPS 100mm faders, 10.5kg unpacked) and confirms this is the analog non-FX ZED-24, distinct from the effects-bearing ZED-12FX/ZED-22FX siblings shown as separate products; neither page mentions phantom power (left null).

products.name: Soundcraft Signature 22 MTK
products.priceNote: US price USD $799, from the Sound on Sound review (published April 2016), "information" section: "$799. Harman Pro" (Harman Pro is Soundcraft's US distributor); the review body also cites "a street price around the £650 $799 mark". The Soundcraft manufacturer page lists no price.
products.provenance: The Soundcraft manufacturer page (soundcraft.com) is titled "Signature 22 MTK" and confirms this exact model via its variant comparison table (22 channels, 16 Ghost preamps, 4-band Sapphyre EQ, 5 auxes, 100mm faders, 2-in/2-out USB with 24-in/22-out on the 22 MTK) plus a Specifications block giving Weight 11.36kg (25.1lb); it publishes no price. The Sound on Sound review (published April 2016) reviews the exact "Signature 22 MTK", corroborating 16 mic preamps, "a total of five aux send buses", and the "24-in/22-out USB audio interface", and states the US price as "$799. Harman Pro" (also "a street price around the £650 $799 mark"). Both pages independently identify the same model, so the model-identity check passes.

products.name: Solid State Logic SiX
products.priceNote: US MSRP $1,799.99 listed on Vintage King (product "SSL SiX Small Format Desktop Mixer", MSRP $1,799.99). Vintage King editorial also cross-references "the SiX ($1799.99)" as distinct from the BiG SiX ($2999.99). The manufacturer page lists no price.
products.provenance: The SSL manufacturer product page (solidstatelogic.com/products/six) confirms this is the plain SiX: an all-analog SuperAnalogue desktop console with two mono SuperAnalogue mic pres, a new two-band channel EQ, a G-Series master bus compressor, two stereo cue buses and 100mm faders, and no USB audio interface. Vintage King's "SSL SiX Small Format Desktop Mixer" listing corroborates the identity ("6-channel desktop analog mixer with 2 SuperAnalogue microphone preamps... 2 mono recording channels, 2 stereo line channels, 2 cue buses") and states a US MSRP of $1,799.99, explicitly distinguished from the BiG SiX at $2,999.99. Note: Vintage King's bulleted "FEATURES" block erroneously copies BiG SiX specs (16-channel USB interface, 3-band EQ, "up to 18 inputs"), so spec values were taken only from the SiX-specific descriptive text and the manufacturer page.

products.name: Rode Rodecaster Pro II
products.priceNote: US price $699. Sound on Sound's August 2022 review lists the US price verbatim as "$699." (RØDE Microphones LLC); Guitar Center lists the RODECaster Pro II at $699.00.
products.provenance: The RØDE US product page (rode.com/en-us/products/rodecaster-pro-ii) confirms the exact model "RØDECaster Pro II": four Neutrik combo inputs with Revolution Preamps, a three-band equaliser per channel, nine individually assignable channels (six physical + three virtual faders), and standalone multitrack/stereo recording to a microSD card. Sound on Sound's dated review (Published August 2022) corroborates the same unit — four analogue mic/line inputs, a three-band EQ, virtual channels 7-9 (nine total), standalone SD/USB recording, and a 16-in/2-out USB audio interface — and states the US price verbatim as "$699." (RØDE Microphones LLC), matching Guitar Center's $699.00 listing. Weight is published only in pounds (4.3 lb), so weightKg is left null; phantom-power granularity, aux sends, onboard-effect count and fader length are not stated verbatim and are null.

products.name: Tascam Mixcast 4
products.priceNote: US price listed verbatim as "$599" in the Sound on Sound review (Published June 2022), attributed to TEAC America — the introductory US price. The manufacturer spec page carries no price.
products.provenance: The manufacturer spec page (tascam.com/us/product/mixcast_4) confirms the exact model "Mixcast 4", stating 4 mic inputs (MIC INPUT jacks 1-4, XLR/TRS combo), a 14in/2out USB audio interface (14 channels output from the unit), direct SD-card multitrack recording up to 14 tracks, and a weight of 2.55 kg; it carries no price. The Sound on Sound review (Published June 2022) independently confirms model identity — 14 recording channels, four mic inputs, and per-channel phantom power engaged via each channel's Condenser preset — and lists the US price verbatim as "$599" from TEAC America. Both pages describe the same Mixcast 4 unit, so model identity is not in doubt; specs left null (totalInputChannels, eqBandsPerChannel, auxSends, builtInEffects, faderLengthMm) were not stated verbatim on either fetched page.

products.name: Zoom PodTrak P8
products.priceNote: US price $549.99, listed verbatim as "$549.99 USD" in The Podcast Consultant's PodTrak P8 review spec chart (and inline "The ZOOM PodTrak P8 ($549.99)"); review originally posted 2023-11-07, updated 2025-10-29. Zoom's official product page showed the unit as "unavailable" with no price listed, so the price is sourced from the dated review rather than the manufacturer page.
products.provenance: Zoom's official PodTrak P8 product page (this exact model, no sibling) carries the full technical spec table verbatim: "NUMBER OF INPUT CHANNELS: Mic inputs: 6 (mono)", "Phantom power +48 V", "Audio interface 44.1 kHz、16-bit、6 in / 2 out", SDHC/SDXC recording media, and "Weight (unit only) 1.43 kg"; the page listed the item as unavailable with no price. The Podcast Consultant's dated review (posted 2023-11-07, updated 2025-10-29) confirms the same PodTrak P8 (6 XLR mic inputs, 70 dB gain, 16-bit/44.1kHz, SD up to 512GB) and states the US price as "$549.99 USD", and notes "Phantom power available on all inputs"; the phantom topology is per-channel per the fetched Hot Rod Cameras listing, which states each of the six mic preamps has "selectable +48V phantom power". usbRecordChannels reflects the manufacturer spec-table figure "6 in / 2 out" (the older marketing bullet "2-input, 2-output USB audio interface" on the same page is superseded by this detailed spec).

products.name: Midas DM16
products.priceNote: US price sourced from Guitar Center (guitarcenter.com), which lists the "Midas DM16 16-Channel Analog Mixer" (Item #1500000050729) at $369.00 USD. The official Midas manufacturer page does not publish a price.
products.provenance: The official Midas product page (midasconsoles.com/en/products/0601-AHA) confirms this exact model — "MIDAS DM16, 16 Input Analogue Live and Studio Mixer" — through its full Architecture & Engineering specification: an analogue design with 12 Midas microphone preamplifiers, global 48V phantom power (single phantom switch feeding each mic input), 3-band mono-channel EQ, 2 aux sends, 60 mm faders and a nominal weight of 5 kg; its complete I/O enumeration lists no USB audio interface and no onboard DSP effects, so both are 0. Guitar Center (US retailer) corroborates model identity and lists the US price of $369.00, with a spec table matching Format Analog, Total inputs 16, Mic preamps 12, Aux sends 2 and EQ bands 3 (its prose text erroneously says "eight" preamps, but its own spec table and the manufacturer page both state 12). No release date is stated on either page, so releaseDate is null.
